marshal-canton-lore-and-dialogue.title: Bounty Hunting - Marshal Canton Lore & Dialogue
marshal-canton-lore-and-dialogue.blurb: Who Marshal Canton is, where to find him, the clues about the man in the machine, and every line he says, laid out as the conversation menus you see in game.

sections.title: Who Is Marshal Canton?
sections.html:
Marshal Canton is the bounty giver for Skyline Valley. He stands at The Trading Post by the Bounty Board and hands out Grunt Hunts and Head Hunts.

{img:canton-trading-post.avif}

He is a robot in a cowboy hat with a glass dome on top, and he introduces himself as "Frank Canton, United States Marshal". He says he was first appointed as a Marshal in Oklahoma in 1894, and that "this whole robot business came later".

He talks like an old Western lawman: outlaws, rustlers, desperadoes, the Law with a capital L. He no longer has a body that can handle rough ground ("this goddarned drive motor"), so he farms the gunslinging out to bounty hunters.

There's no pay from him, because "the governor ain't exactly been filling the kitty lately". You keep whatever you loot. Head Hunt contracts, though, cost a {posterPrice}-cap "charitable donation".

Is he really Frank Canton?

Push him on his past and the act cracks. With Intelligence 12+ you can tell him the real Frank Canton died in the 1920s. Ask him to explain and he breaks down mid-sentence: "Oh, God, what've they done to me? Where am I? What happened to the spa?" Then he snaps back and refuses to talk about it.

{img:canton-personal-questions.avif}

The Scan 14: Josiah Harrison holotape from A Matter of Matter (Rapidan Camp) has Canton's voice in it. Iggy Stolz tells him: "You're not even really you, just a miscalibration of a has-been actor." Canton answers "Actor? What kind of..." and goes into the same pained "Where am I? Why can't I see anything?" breakdown.

Put together, it looks like the brain in the robot was scanned from someone who played Frank Canton, and the personality took over. The tape's title names Josiah Harrison. He never says this in one line, so treat it as a reading of the clues rather than a stated fact.

Little details

  • He hums "Camptown Races" while idle, keeps losing his hat ("Got a powerful need for some more glue") and can't remember where he got it.
  • "Nothing like fresh air. Be real nice if I could still smell it."
  • He greets you differently if you're a ghoul the first time you meet.
  • He has worked "with every cattle baron, sheriff's office, Pinkerton, and governor from Wyoming to Texas".

sections.title: Where to Find Him
sections.html: The Trading Post, Skyline Valley, next to the Bounty Board.

sections.title: Quests & Activities
sections.html:
• Skyline Valley Grunt Hunts and Head Hunts. If you've already finished a Burning Springs Grunt Hunt you can skip most of his pitch with "You mean bounty hunting."
  • Chasing A Lead. Bring him the strange coded message and he decodes it, explaining that outlaws hide messages in slang and code.
  • A Matter of Matter. His voice is on the Scan 14 holotape (see Lore Documents).

sections.title: Buying a Wanted Poster
sections.html:
He sells Skyline Valley Wanted Posters through his conversation, not a shop menu. The full steps with pictures are on the Skyline Valley Head Hunt Guide.

  1. First time: "You must have something more challenging than these bounties." → "So, tell me about these “desperadoes”." → "I'll take one of these premium contracts." → "[5,000 Caps] Here's your “donation.”"
  2. After that: "I'm looking for a premium contract." → "[5,000 Caps] Here's your “donation.”"

You need {posterPrice} caps on you, and he won't sell one while you already carry a Skyline Valley Wanted Poster.

sections.title: Who Is The Ghoul?
sections.html:
The Ghoul runs bounty hunting in Burning Springs. He works out of The Last Resort, the saloon in Highway Town, and hands out Grunt Hunts and Head Hunts from a stack of contracts.

He is Cooper Howard from the Fallout TV series, voiced by Walton Goggins, and arrived with the Burning Springs update (per Bethesda).

What he lets slip

  • He isn't from Ohio, and he isn't saying where he's from: "Where I'm from is one of those things that's not your concern."
  • He's here for a reason: "Let's just say I followed somebody out here. Somebody I'd very much like to meet."
  • He's been looking into the Vaults. He tells a fresh Vault 76 dweller he "already interrogated the last one of you to come out of that hole. Sounds like there's nothing down there for me."
  • He doesn't care what a target did, "so long as the caps from the bounty end up in my pocket to pay for the chems in my lungs." He stays at The Last Resort because "the barkeep here's got the vials I like".
  • On the Rust King: "Not the first would-be king I've seen in the Wasteland. Doubt he'll be the last... All I know is kings fall, and all crowns rust."
  • His one rule for bounty hunters: "We don't do 'dead or alive'. Just dead."

In the TV show he's searching for his family, which fits "followed somebody out here". Nothing in Fallout 76 names who he's following, though.

sections.title: Where to Find Him
sections.html:
His home is The Last Resort, the saloon in Highway Town, Burning Springs. He stands against the back wall.

Before you've been to Burning Springs, he can also turn up in every region of Appalachia, standing over a target he's just killed. He tells you about Burning Springs ("burnt clean away after the war"), points you to the bridge by Point Pleasant, and says to find him at The Last Resort.

{spawns}

sections.title: Buying a Wanted Poster
sections.html:
Burning Springs Wanted Posters are bought from him through dialogue, not a shop menu:

  1. First time: "Got anything better than these grunts?" → "Tell me about these “juicy” targets." → "Give me a premium target." → "[5,000 Caps] All right, here's your caps."
  2. After that: "Give me a premium target." → "[5,000 Caps] All right, here's your caps."

You need {posterPrice} caps on you. If you already have a Burning Springs Wanted Poster: "No can do, hoss. One per customer."

sections.title: Who Is Minerva?
sections.html:
Minerva is the Blue Ridge Caravan Company's travelling plan merchant. She sells hand-drawn "recreations" of rare plans and recipes at a discount, and she only stays in one place for a short time before moving on.

{img:minerva-caravan.avif}

Her story, in her own words

"Been with 'em since I was pint sized brainy brat. I'm originally from DC. Survived the bombs thanks to my local library seconding as a bomb shelter. Wound up wandering from group to group, until my talents caught the eye of some Blue Ridge folk passing through. Ended up being an apprentice for a book salesman, rewriting books by hand. He was a dear friend and great mentor. After he passed, I took over his caravan. Switched from books to something a little more catered for the modern survivor's needs, though. But Blue Ridge are my business partners and my family... And I couldn't ask for a better one."

The human copying machine

She has a photographic memory: "If I've seen it, I can picture it, and draw it exactly so." Everything she sells is drawn from memory, which is also why her stock keeps changing ("I can only draw so much before my wrist snaps in two. Not many treatments for carpal tunnel syndrome in the Wasteland").

Ask whether it's a waste of her talent and she's blunt: "Turning a profit is all I know, and I ever want to know."

Tommy Ten-Toes and Minos

Tommy Ten-Toes is her ghoul bodyguard. He's quick to point out he works for Blue Ridge, not Minerva, "but seeing as I only ever gets paired wit Minerva, I guess it don' make much difference." They used to call him Tommy the Nose; now it's Ten-Toes "on accounts of my ten toes... on the one foot" (fifteen in total, he works out). He misses zoos, loves rhinoceroses, and something happened "in Chattanooga. That poor lil' doggie..."

Minerva's take on him: "He may seem intimidating, but he's a big goofy teddy bear... Try and steal something, though, and he will rip your sternum out. I've seen him do it."

Her brahmin is called Minos.

She first appeared in the Steel Reign update, and the Fallout Wiki credits Erikka J. Veney as her voice.

sections.title: Where to Find Her
sections.html:
Minerva, Tommy and Minos are placed at four spots, and only one is switched on at a time: Foundation, The Crater, Fort Atlas and The Whitespring Resort. She has her own shout-out lines for The Crater, Foundation and Fort Atlas.

See Minerva's Lists for what she sells on each visit, and the Gold Bullion Calculator.

minerva-lore-and-dialogue.loreIntro: Notes that mention her. The caravan manifest in Out of the Blue lists her as "Minerva - Merchant (Plans, Recipes)", travelling with Aries as guard and Tommy Ten-Toes off duty.

sections.title: Who Is Aries?
sections.html:
Aries is a caravan guard for the Blue Ridge Caravan Company, working out of Big Bend Tunnel. He wears a mask, talks in grim jokes, and gives a little sermon before a fight ("Let's hope no one is going to any graves today... Other than our enemies").

{img:aries-big-bend.avif}

Aries is Calvin van Lowe

His real name is Calvin van Lowe, the Lewisburg cryptid hunter behind the Imposter Sheepsquatch. He says it himself on the last Protocol Adonais tape, recorded for Carver: "My name is Calvin van Lowe. I'm the brother of your mom, Shelley. I know she ain't your birth mom, but that still makes you family."

Before the war he worked for the Bysshe company under the codename "Blacksheep". A Bysshe psychiatric evaluation calls his mental acuity "extremely high" but notes "a dissociative view of the social world". He tells you Bysshe "wanted Lewisburg for some natural gas deposit under it or something", and faking Sheepsquatch sightings was part of the job.

He reprogrammed assaultrons to play the Sheepsquatch (the Behavioral Reprogramming tape and the Assembly Platform session logs). One of them turned on him, which is why he wears the mask: "Play with killer robots, get your face ripped off... Can't breathe without this thing now."

His sister Shelley reported him missing and put up "Wanted: Sheepsquatch" notices, though she doubted he was really eaten.

Life as Aries

He took the name Aries and worked the Blue Ridge routes in Kentucky. On Protocol Adonais #4, Eugenie asks why he came back to Appalachia after all that time on the Kentucky routes. His answer: "Family."

Carver Timmerman, a Blue Ridge merchant, is his step-nephew. Carver finds Aries unsettling and asked Joanna Mayfield not to be paired with him; her discarded reply turns him down ("I know Aries is a strange fellow, but we don't have enough guards to accommodate personal preference"). After Protocol Adonais he left a letter for Shelley with Carver, but says he doesn't "have the courage to face Shelley in person just yet".

He turns up in other places too: the Middle Mountain Pitstop terminal says "that Aries feller" planned a critter repeller that ended up attracting critters, and Vinny Costa's terminal has a complaint from him: "Vinny, why don't you like me?"

He first appeared in Wastelanders. The Lying Lowe, Baa Baa Black Sheep and The Lowe-Down quests tell the Calvin side of the story (per the Fallout Wiki).

sections.title: Where to Find Him
sections.html: Big Bend Tunnel, by the Blue Ridge Caravan Company office. He's one of the guards who can run the Riding Shotgun activity, and he travels to Harpers Ferry Tunnel with you and Paladin Rahmani in Out of the Blue.

sections.title: Quests & Activities
sections.html:
• Out of the Blue (main quest): he guides you and Paladin Rahmani through Harpers Ferry Tunnel to look for missing caravanners.
  • Protocol Adonais (side quest): he sends you after his Protocol Adonais holotapes, then asks you to burn the last one or give it to Carver.
  • Activity: Riding Shotgun: one of the possible caravan guards through Big Bend Tunnel.
